title: Award in Perm and Straightening of Hair
description:
Perming and straightening hair are much requested services. It is important as a hairdresser to be able to permanently change the hair structure by perming,  straightening or relaxing it
Apply perm lotion,  time the process,  Perm hair to achieve a variety of textures and curls after accurate consultation; carry out tests that are necessary before,  during and after the process; select the correct strength of product and the proper tools for the service; use pre-perm or pre-treatment e.g. Porosity equaliser if needed; wind perm rollers in a variety of ways to achieve different effects; apply perm/ straightening product and time the process accurately; rinse properly to remove all product and removing excess water before applying neutraliser; apply neutraliser to complete the treatment and time it accurately and rinse it out well; remove perm rods carefully without disturbing curls formation; carry out the necessary styling; straighten and relax hair following the manufacturer’s instructions when using scalp protector,  when needed; give advice that ensures the result is maintained and follow salon regulations with regards to health and safety at all times The learner will be able to perm hair to achieve a variety of textures and curls; straighten and relax hair after adequate consultation; section and wind hair according to the desired effect; perform tests needed before during and at the end of the processing; apply perm/straightening prodcut and time the process accurately; negative consequences of ignoring to consider the above; the different types of sectioning and winding techniques and rod size for perming the hair; the different procedures for straightening relaxing and smoothing hair; title: VET Award in Plumbing
description:

title: Skills2Care  Core Principles in Dementia Care Award
description:
Over  the years there has been a marked increase in older adults  being  diagnosed  with a  change  in cognitive function,  or a dementia. title: Award in Wines
description:

title: Award in Enhancing Employability: Communication and Presentation Skills
description:
The communication and presentation skills course is aimed to upgrade and polish the abilities of future employees. The course exhibits the importance and need of communicating effectively to render effective presentations. The employment trend to be flexible, calls for, the improvement of the social intelligence, presentation and public speaking skills to control nerves and build the confidence needed.
Analyse the audience needs. Get the audience attention. Master the delivery of the speech/presentation. Make use of microphones and visual aids. Overcome fear and nervousness. Make an impact at various meetings/presentations. Show effectiveness in debates. Understand the concepts of attitude in communication. Think positively to communicate confidently. Using non-verbal communication to interact better with the audience. Communicate the facts and eliminating biases. Aware of the emotions that may arise during communication and be able to direct these emotions to make the speech/presentation to stick. Plan, compose and revise the intended speech/presentation. title: Award in English for Diplomatic Purposes
description:

The learner will be able to demonstrate a variety of english language skills and knowledge of diplomacy which they can adopt whilst working at a European level an further promote within their own trade union activity at national level; apply the content from this experience with colleagues at a national level and with greater ease. title: Diploma in Fish Husbandry
description:
This programme of studies introduces the learner to the basics of fish husbandry and provides the knowledge and skills required by the learner for eventual employment in related industries such as the fish farming and aquatics industries. Being the only course in Malta that is solely dedicated to fish husbandry,  this programme offers an excellent opportunity for employment in this industry,  which has now become an important economic sector in the Maltese Islands. The learner will develop the knowledge and practical skills needed,  provided that one attends all the practical sessions which are vital to enhance the theoretical knowledge gained during lectures.
Perform simple techniques in pet fish care Perform simple techniques in fish handling and feeding Make use of standard tools and equipment in line with safety procedures. Perform monitoring and simple analysis of water for fish farming and pet fish breeding

title: Award in International Film Making with Bollywood
description:
This course is to ensure filmmaking can be done at an international level adapting Bollywood techniques. This is to make sure the learners of this course will have a fully comprehensive vocational training where they can learn the aspects of filmmaking from scratch to completing a film shoot with the required post production as well as being able to market and promote the film.

This course is to provide the learner with hands on teaching, in theory and in practice of film making. The course is designed giving the learner ALL the aspects required in International filmmaking with Bollywood.

The course will cover areas and values in Bollywood filmaking such as dance , 
music and songs and adapting them to International Filmmaking. Bollywood is one of the leading film industries in the world. This course is designed so Bollywood techniques can be applied to International standards of filmmaking and vice-versa. 

The course will be able to give the learner a positive impact of filmmaking once the course has been completed. Furthermore, the learner should be able to fully understand (at an intermediate level) of being involved in the film industry in both the East and the West.

This will be a vocational course with lectures, seminars and tutorials inbetween the modules to help the learner achieve their full target.

The main concept of this course is for the learner to work as part of a group and have a finished short film made. The short film they will start from the beginning, where they will be part of writing the script. Once the script is written they will look into all the aspects of making this script into a complete film, this will involve them understanding all the requirements and professions and skills to make this film. They will work alongside experienced film industry workers from Malta, UK, USA and Bollywood, and be taught and given details on how to produce the film. They will get all support from pre-production to production to post-production and final classes will be given on distribution, marketing and promotions of the film. Throughout the course and during modules the learners will be assessed by the staff and guided so the final product, a short film is made to International standards with Bollywood techniques as and when required.
The learner will be able to: 

a) Understand each module of the course and then be able to apply the skills for future learning or in this case mostly to be used within the film or television industry.

b) Plan for the future - in getting to further higher education in any of the related courses in filmmaking

c) Pursue a career in filmaking The learner will be able to: 

a) To be able to communicate with filmmaking industry workers – This will be done throughout the course while interacting with the various parties involved when making the film in stages. 

b) To be able to communicate with other learners as part of a team, starting from scriptwriting and sharing ideas. Will be communicating new ideas and innovations during the course while making the film.

c) To be able to communicate with marketing and promoting the film with festivals and distributors.

title: MQF Level 3 Award in Concepts of Music, Dance, Drama & Visual Art
description:
This module is intended to give an overview of the underlying concepts of each artistic medium as well as a brief historical outline of each.
At the end of the module/unit the learner will have acquired the following skills: 

a) Analyse the components of works of art from different art forms. 
b) Efficiently interact with other artists through knowledge of the terminology employed in the different art forms.
c) Appreciate works of art from all the 4 different art forms from different periods in history. 
d) Historically place a work of art from the 4 different art forms. 
e) Place the idiom and style of a work of art from the 4 different art forms. At the end of the module/unit the learner will have been exposed to the following: 

a) The basic concepts and terminology of the 4 different art forms
b) The aesthetics of the 4 different art forms
c) How these concepts and aesthetics are demonstrated in masterpieces from different eras of art history
d) An overview of the history of the 4 different art forms and the impact of main figures in the development of that art form At the end of the module/unit the learner will have acquired the responsibility and autonomy to:

a) Understand the aesthetics and dynamics of the 4 different forms of art.
b) Collaborate with artists from a different area then theirs through understanding of the basic concepts of that art form. 
c) Understand the different terminology used in the different art forms.
d) Discuss with artists from different artistic areas as how the collaboration can be more productive.

title: Award in Work Ethics, Rights and Responsibilities for Housekeepers
description:
This unit is aimed at providing the knowledge and skills required to carry out housekeeping work in an ethical and professional manner. It delves into the key principles of work ethics in relation to fellow workers and customers. The unit also informs learners about employer and employee rights and responsibilities and organisational procedures.
a)	Outline employee and employer rights and responsibilities under employment law, including Disability Discrimination Act, Health and Safety and other relevant legislation.
b)	Understand the difference between ethics and law and ensure that both legal and ethical standards are followed at all times. 
c)	Identify the key ethical principles of housekeeping. 
d)	Maintain a professional attitude with customers and show courtesy. 
e)	Maintain a cordial relationship with colleagues and management. 
b)	Respect work obligations, duties and responsibilities, whilst also respecting one’s own rights. 
c)	Show tolerance and acceptance to diversity. 
d)	Tackle unexpected and challenging situations professionally whilst recognising the importance of seeking the help of superiors when necessary. a)	State importance of having employment rights and responsibilities.
b)	Describe organisational procedures for Health and Safety, including documentation.
c)	Describe organisational procedures for equality and diversity including documentation.
d)	Understand the definition of work ethics and its  importance in everyday work life.
e)	Provide examples of work ethics. 
f)	Discuss the impact of a lack of work ethics on customers, workers and the orgaisation.
g)	Understand the importance of accepting diversity on the basis of opinion, knowledge, ability, race, gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religion etc. Applying knowledge and understanding
The learner will be able to:
a)	Value diverse guests equally and maintain professionalism and courtesy with all guests at all times. 
b)	Value diverse colleagues equally and maintain an professional attitude towards all employees. 
c)	Recognise boundaries and ensure that one’s behaviour respects those boundaries at all times. 
d)	Retain confidentiality of customers at all times. 
e)	Respect guests and guests’ property and engage in appropriate and ethical behaviour at all times. 
f)	Remain calm and act professionally when confronted with challenging situations. 
g)	Maintain a professional work ethic even when superiors and colleagues are not around and thus there is no supervision.

title: Water Awareness and Rescue Concepts Award
description:
The objective of the course is for those learners  who want to learn basic water rescue  skills. Topics undertaking in this course are regarded by the Health & safety executive as being important in maintaining good practice in the safe,  prompt and effective treatment of injuries and ill health in at the beach. The course provides learners with the knowledge,  understanding and skills in  water rescue senarios
Appreciate the role and responsibilities of a rescuer. Understand and realise why responders act accordingly to a variety of aquatic accidents and injuries including an unresponsive casualty who is breathing normally at sea and on land,  as well as an unresponsive casualty who is not breathing normally at sea and on land. Fully comprehend and aware why panicked swimmers are managed in such a way. Value the assessment of recognising and assisting a casualty who is drowning. Realise and fully understand why rescuers use various recue equipment: throw line,  life ring,  rescue tube,  rescue can. Undertake further studies so as to gain information and knowledge on  water rescue Communicate with others ,  during an accident scene. Martian dialogue with  members of the emergency services present at the scene of an accident. Listen to patients needs. Be able to express his opinion and discuss issues.  Be able to share knowledge.  Be able to provide instruction to others re actions to be taken in an given situation.  Promote proper interaction  with others so as to coordinate help during an accident. Promote proper interaction  with  the police,  AFM and CPD as needed.  Provide suitable care to injured persons. Demonstrate competence in the analysis and practice of ethical communication.  Describe  the importance of body language when dealing with injured person or interacting with family/crowd. Reports and maintain records of findings and actions carried out.  Convey  proper information to other professionals.

title: Cross Cultural Communication
description:
This training course aims to develop the language and communicative skills for individuals and workers who are in a multi-cultural environment. Through exploration of a variety of language and communicative techniques,  participants of this course will develop their ability to implement the RADAR method
The learner will be able to explain an awareness of culture and recognise its varieties in different nationalities; recognise and identify stereotypical attitudes which can damage the term’s ambiance; identify and address the do’s and don’ts of cultural integration; recognise and analyse different verbal and non-verbal communication to avoid negative impact; adopt a common language within a multi-cultural environment and devise and write a charter of good practices This training course aims to develop the language and communicative skills for individuals and workers who are in a multi-cultural environment. Through exploration of a variety of language and communicative techniques,  participants of this course will develop their ability to implement the RADAR method. This particular course will have an in-depth focus on various levels of conversational and speaking skills,  using a high level of lexical material and themes,  and therefore would be recommended for participants who are confident speakers of the English language as a second language – the recommended level of applicants would be approximately CEFR B1 (or above.) During this week long intensive course participants will take part in a range of activities which will allow them to exhibit their existing knowledge of dealing with problem solving  and conflict resolution scenarios,  but also to create a cultural awareness which will enable them  to enhance their acquired skills so as to ensure they continue to handle difficult situations with an appropriate and sensitive approach By the end of this training activity participants will improve their ability to look at existing differences in a non-biased and more open-minded manner and be better able to resolve such conflicts through discussions. The participants will expand their language knowledge of certain English language expressions and terms which can be crucial to resolving scenarios of conflict. By participating in this course participants will improve their awareness of commonly encountered cultural differences within a European community and be better able to strategize how to overcome these differences and lead to better integration of different cultures within the working environment

title: VET Award in Refrigeration and Air-Conditioning
description:
This course is aimed at providing the learner with knowledge,  skills and competences required to work as Refrigeration and Air-conditioning Maintenance Personnel. Through this training programme,  the learner will be able to identify and understand the correct practices used in this industry. It is also aimed at raising a sense of Health & Safety,  Environmental Awareness,  Customer Service and Work Communication.
Describe the direct and indirect methods for checking an RAC system. Explain how to make visual and manual inspections of the whole system. Explain the most important and basic environment regulations and procedures related to handling,  storage and transportation of refrigerant and oils. Discuss faults found within a RAC system. Interpret a Pressure Enthalpy Chart,  a psychometric chart and refrigeration cycles. Name the different components of a RAC system. Interact with peers and customers. Discuss project requirements with clients and peers. Write and review project quotations for prospective clients.  Apply health and safety procedures to ensure a safe working practice in this industry. Check for leaks (provided it does not entail breaking into the system). Follow environmental regulations related to refrigerants. Install,  perform maintenance and service units in an environmentally friendly approach. Understand basic thermodynamics. Undertake further studies to obtain the category II or I licence.

title: Diploma in Applied Science

The learner will be able to understand the fundamental principles and laws of science,  and how these are applied within the industrial sector. The learner will also be able to understand the science of different materials,  and gain an awareness of the principles behind certain technologies.
Understand the impact of human activity on the environment Investigate forces,  motion,  energy,  light,  electricity and sound waves Identify chemical substances and organic compounds. Describe the factors that can affect and control human health

title: Award in Sustainable Use of Plant Protection Products for Distributors
description: In this course learners will be trained on the major legislation related to PPPs together with the risks and hazards related to handling,  use and storage of these products. The unit will then proceed to cover human and environmental health related to PPPs and how such products should be used safely and efficiently.

title: Award in Green Jobs Motivational Training
description:
The programme is intended to sensitize participants to the country’s transition towards a more resilient and sustainable environment.  In this sense it will guide a discussion on the prevailing environmental issues Malta has to face and why we need to transition to a more sustainable and circular economy.  In doing so it will be demonstrated how sustainable development does not relate solely to physical development but how it involves the maximisation of economic, social and environmental goals in all forms of development.  The training will explain what green jobs are and how they can contribute to the restoration of the environment and to social equity as well as how they can form part of Malta’s new economic model. Using a series of participatory mapping exercises, small group discussions and presentations, the learners will be encouraged to share their ideas on green jobs within the local job market, identify key skills that are needed to carry out such jobs and discuss their expectations in terms of career prospects following this training.
The learner will be able to: 

General skills:
•	Participate in group discussions and brainstorming sessions on the importance and growing need of green jobs, on the prevailing environmental issues, and on ways in which green jobs aid in overcoming specific environmental issues 
•	Design and deliver a presentation on green jobs and their contribution towards overcoming environmental issues 


Specific skills
•	Identify gaps in their knowledge and competences that hinder them from applying for and obtaining a job in the green economy.
•	Design a personal plan of action with the goal of pursuing a green job
•	Assess how they can contribute towards overcoming environmental issues through their employment in green jobs  
•	Identify the skills required by different skills jobs
•	Establish their own skills gap to underaking a particular green job and the relative learning required thereto The learner will be able to: 
a)	Fully comprehend and understand their roles and responsibilities should they be employed in a green job
b)	Provide a definition of a green job
c)	Reflect on what they have learnt and on how it affected their initial understanding of green jobs 
d)	Identify what role they may be able to take up in the green economy 
e)	Identify which information, skills and tools acquired through the core training modules will assist them in their green job 
f)	Understand the prevailing environmental issues and how such issues necessitate interventions of green jobs
g)	Understand the environmental challenges faced by Malta and the skills required for such challenges to be overcome

title: Award in Safe, Hygienic and Secure Working Environments in Hospitality
description:
This module focuses on the principles and importance of Health and Safety issues within the Hospitality environment with special reference to Housekeeping duties that is cleaning of rooms, lobbies, restaurants and other places within hotels and apartments as part of the hospitality industry. Moreover, it emphasizes on the principles of Personal Protection Equipment, Infection Control, Hygiene, etc. 

This module will develop students’ knowledge to enable them to work in and maintain a safe, hygienic and secure working environment. They will develop their knowledge on the principles of good personal hygiene and how these impacts on health and safety in the workplace. They will gain an understanding of common hazards, types of emergencies and reasons for first aid in the workplace. They will also explore the importance of fire and security procedures.
The Learner will be able to: 

a) Follow health, safety and security regulations such and apply it to the workplace.
b) Recognise hazards in the work place and adapts own work practices to ensure safety and hygiene.
c) Gain knowledge about own responsibilities and adapts own behaviour to apply work practises that ensure the health and safety of oneself and others in the working environment.

title: MQF Level 3 Award in Excelerate
description:
The ‘Excelerate’, course is meant as a self enhancement programme to learners for their own internal use and not for public use. 

This course is a collection of learning solutions aimed to support businesses acquire digital skills to enhance further their business. 

The Excelerate course consists of seven modules which are required to be followed consecutively as listed in this accreditation application form.    whereby each module aims to provide business owners or aspiring new business owners, with the opportunity to build up new digital competences that will help them improve and ameliorate their position, presence and business engagement when online. 

All seven course modules are to be successfully followed and completed, to gain MQF Level 3 Award in Excelerate.
At the end of the module/unit the learner will acquire the following skills: 

a)	Apply the newly acquired technologies, to his business so as to affirm further his business to the different demands requested by the market;

b)	Make a thorough assessment of the digital performance of his business and the ability to transform his organization into a more efficient one.

c)	Using ERP within your business can be beneficial in terms of cost saving and providing you assistance in the identification of unwanted wastage within your business. 
*
d)	Provide learners with a sound vision of the different benefits that may be reaped when investing in a suitable system relevant to his business.

e)	The ability to carry out a business impact assessment to determine which are at most risk of being exposed to a cyber-attack.

f)	Provide learners with the technological knowledge of the different available tools required to create and design a webpage.

g)	Compose and amend the leadership style into the real working environment through the organizational skills acquired in the virtual world. At the end of this module/unit, the learner will have been exposed to: 

a)	Review the business idea and adapt digital strategy within his business.

b)	Provide learners with a taste of the technologically driven sectors available in the business sector. 

c)	Apply the actual planning and execution systems of the ERP and provide learners with better knowledge when selecting the best ERP relevant to their business.

d)	Improves the efficiency within the business in its different terms, ranging from sales, marketing, product development and even financially. 

e)	Understand that an attractive website, although it may have positive effects on your business, may make your business prone to cyber-attacks.

f)	Detailed definition of the core web design language, that need to be mastered, to control the structure of pages and understand the different possibilities that each of the core skills can give to your web design. 

g)	The ability to choose a collaborative platform as a replacement of the disparate range of systems used, as a way to facilitate employees’ work and effort. At the end of these lessons, learners will have acquired the responsibility and autonomy to:

a)	Deal and manage with the ‘digital disruption’ encountered and consider change as a ‘gift’ instead of an ‘issue’ within business. Learn to negotiate with new market challenges to retain his business at equal level within the competing environment. 

b)	Learn about the different migration paths available and those that appeal most to your business, whilst gaining the ability to exploit opportunities presented by current dynamic business environments and evolving technologies.

title: VET award in intermediate Gas Metal Arc Welding
description:
This course is aimed to provide the learner with general knowledge,  skills and competence required to work in the steel and fabrication industry as a welder. The learner will acquire skills to produce welds in different positions using the MAG and FCAW processes. Through this training programme,  the learner will obtain knowledge on the principles of the GMAW,  its parameters,  applications and consumables. Through practicum,  the student will acquire the skillset required to produce structural welds in the horizontal and vertical positions,  using the MAG and FCAW processes. Furthermore,  the learner will gain knowledge on metallurgical properties of metals and methods to conserve these properties during welding. Moreover,  upon completion of this course,  the learner will be able to identify,  prevent and/or take remedial action to remove any weld discontinuity.
Talk to others using technical and correct terms to convey information effectively,  illustrate weld defects to co-workers and superiors by means of sketches and drawings,  read welding inspector’s report and repair any noted discontinuities accordingly,  relay information to co-workers regarding the importance of good weld preparation with regard to material failure due to flaws in design,  explain to co-workers the required precautionary measures needed to prevent hydrogen entrapment in a weldment,  express safety concerns to co-workers and superiors when working in unsafe working environments,  listen and evaluate co-worker’s and superior’s instructions. Carry out independent research using various sources related to permissibility levels of different weld discontinuities,  proceed in undertaking further courses related to NDT,  proceed in furthering own welding skills in order to reduce discontinuities in the weldment,  proceed in furthering own knowledge on the weldability properties of different ferrous and non-ferrous metals,  proceed in furthering own practical knowledge and skills on different methods used of pre-heating and monitoring the interpass temperature,  proceed in furthering own welding skills (in terms of hand-eye coordination,  endurance & the ability of a steady hand),  gain confidence in own ability to weld in different welding positions and different joint designs,  learn both the theoretical and practical necessities to perform sound welds,  carry out independent research using various sources related to permissibility levels of different weld discontinuities,  proceed in furthering own welding skills in order to reduce discontinuities in the weldment

title: Water Rescue and Lifesaving Technician Award
description:
The objective of the programme is for those learners  who want to learn lifeguarding skills,  or want to perform duties as part of a water rescue team. Topics undertaking in this course are regarded by the Health & safety executive as being important in maintaining good practice in the safe,  prompt and effective treatment of injuries and ill health in at the beach. Communicate with others ,  during an accident scene; Martian dialogue with  members of the emergency services present at the scene of an accident; Listen to patients needs; Be able to express his opinion and discuss issues; Be able to share knowledge; Be able to provide instruction to others re actions to be taken in an given situation; Promote proper interaction  with others so as to coordinate help during an accident; Promote proper interaction  with  the police,  AFM and CPD as needed; Provide suitable care to injured persons; demonstrate competence in the analysis and practice of ethical communication; Describe  the importance of body language when dealing with injured person or interacting with family/crowd; Reports and maintain records of findings and actions carried out; Convey  proper information to other professionals; Finally acquire lifelong skills to lookout for further information to keep up-to-date on emergency procedures including CPR,  head and spinal injuries,  burns,  scalds,  chest injuries and eye injuries and other major illnesses like chest pain,  anaphylaxis,  stroke,  epilepsy and asthma Appreciate further the role and responsibilities of a lifeguard as learners will become aware and be able to further investigate and broaden their knowledge; Fully understand and become aware and appreciative of how incident assess is done during an incident and justify the actions performed as well as the quality of first aid provided for a variety of injuries; Justify the response given in response to a variety of aquatic accidents and injuries when these happen in the future as learner can pursue their knowledge while appreciating actions taken by responders. This also applies to procedures taken to manage an unresponsive casualty who is breathing normally at sea and on land,  as well as procedures taken to manage an unresponsive casualty who is not breathing normally at sea and on land; Understand,  justify and appreciate through further investigation and study what actions are taken to manage a casualty suffering from spinal injuries in water too deep to stand in; Further their knowledge as learners better understand panicked swimmers and the dynamics of assisting a casualty who is drowning,  or with external traumatic bleeding,  or with a spinal injury in water to deep to stand in;	Understand further through investigation the rationale behind basic rescues by means of a RHIB,  effects of shock,  search techniques through appreciate the need of each; Appreciate and remain up-to-date with different radio communications,  calling for help,  emergency numbers,  different rescue equipment,  essential information one should provide to the emergency team,  evolving responsibilities,  contents of first aid kits through reading and by undertaking further studies so as to gain information and knowledge on lifeguarding

title: Award in Pedicure Treatments
description:
This course will cover the essential topics  required for a person to work as a beauty therapist safely, effectively and independently. 
It covers theoretical underpinning knowledge required to work safely, as well as practical competences required to work safely and effectively in this industry. 4. Devise a treatment plan.

6. Give after care advise.
